canada.title: Hearing may not see 'full scope' of pain caused by daughter's death after dental procedure, family says
canada.summary: The family of a young woman who died after a dental procedure at a southern Manitoba clinic say they have concerns about an upcoming inquiry hearing after sections were removed from prepared statements about how her death affected them.

canada.title: Bains faces serious challenge rebuilding Ontario's Liberal party, insiders say
canada.summary: Navdeep Bains has been elected Ontario's new Liberal leader, taking over a party that has been in the political wilderness for almost a decade. He admits there will be "no shortcuts" back to power.

canada.title: How London homeowners can get up to $1,000 per tree for maintenance
canada.summary: London homeowners can apply for funding to help cover the cost of maintaining mature trees, with the city offering up to $1,000 per tree through its Tree Canopy Conservation Program.

canada.title: Monarch butterfly tagged in N.B. survived fierce challenges before reaching Mexico
canada.summary: After crossing the Bay of Fundy and the Gulf of Maine, and going through a nor’easter and a hurricane, a monarch butterfly weighing less than a gram is closing in on its winter destination in central Mexico.

canada.title: Parole denial for 'chameleon' sex offender by N.Y. board welcomed by Halifax victim
canada.summary: William Shrubsall committed a string of violent sex attacks and other crimes in Halifax in the mid-to-late 1990s and remains imprisoned in New York state. He was extradited from Canada in 2019 to serve prison time there, but because of sentencing guidelines, he was expected to be released before now.

canada.title: Frustrated? Angry? Why these Nova Scotians say you should scream it out
canada.summary: A group of Nova Scotians now meet weekly to scream their frustrations into the ocean. From grocery prices to global instability, they say there's plenty to motivate them these days.

canada.title: Can the N.L. House of Assembly do better? MHAs address challenges in passing legislation
canada.summary: Newfoundland and Labrador's House of Assembly has seen disputes this fall over its operations and procedures, some raised by members and raised by people on outside the legislature with an interest in the proceedings. Members say some of the answers are in the hands of government, but others stem from established norms and traditions the government alone doesn't control.

canada.title: Removal of Baltic III could be nearing completion, Coast Guard says
canada.summary: Work to remove the MSC Baltic III from the rocks of Cedar Cove could soon near completion, according to the Canadian Coast Guard.

canada.title: Will Canadian workers refuse to handle Israeli goods? Why unions increasingly say they should
canada.summary: A movement to cut off Israeli goods is spreading across Canada's unions. The Canadian Labour Congress, which represents more than 3 million workers, passed a resolution last month declaring trade, services and relationships with Israel to be “hot cargo," emphasizing a call for workers to refuse to handle weapons and military equipment destined for Israel.

canada.title: How the Alberta government could fill a new pipeline with royalties paid in oil
canada.summary: To overcome one of the biggest challenges facing Premier Danielle Smith’s ambitions to build a large oil export pipeline to the West Coast, the Alberta government could decide to fill the pipeline with oil collected as royalties from industry.

canada.title: WhatsApp is a 'lifeline' for refugees. Advocates fear it could be severed in fight over federal bill
canada.summary: Meta said this week that Bill C-22 could force it to "consider" withdrawing encrypted services like WhatsApp from Canada. Rights advocates say that would cut refugees and other newcomers off from a key platform they rely on to get information and stay connected to relatives back home.

lines: Good morning. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.

Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, has invited the right-wing Likud party of caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu for coalition talks, his party said on Saturday.

Ontario Liberals have elected Navdeep Bains as the party’s new leader after a marathon nine-month leadership race, with Bains emerging as victor less than one percentage point ahead of his next closest competitor, provincial caucus member Lee Fairclough, The Canadian Press reports.
Alleged Mexican drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ arrested in special forces raid, The Guardian reports.
Swedish Gripen pilot unable to shoot down suspected Russian missile over Poland due to poor weather, commander says, Kyiv Independent reports.
Masked immigration officers arrested two passengers on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as people were boarding Saturday, The Associated Press reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
